facts: Two main classes of approaches have been studied to perform monocular nonrigid 3D reconstruction.
The two main classes of approaches to perform monocular nonrigid 3D reconstruction are Template-based methods and Non-rigid Structure from Motion techniques.
Template-based methods have been applied to reconstruct poorly-textured surfaces.
Template-based methods assume the availability of a 3D shape model prior to reconstruction.
Non-rigid Structure from Motion techniques do not require a shape template.
Non-rigid Structure from Motion techniques rely on points being tracked throughout a video sequence.
Non-rigid Structure from Motion techniques are ill-suited to handle poorly-textured surfaces.
The paper introduces a template-free approach to reconstructing a poorly-textured, deformable surface.
The paper's approach leverages surface isometry.
The paper formulates 3D reconstruction as the joint problem of non-rigid image registration and depth estimation.
The paper's approach yields much more accurate 3D reconstructions than state-of-the-art techniques.
Template-based methods have been studied to perform monocular nonrigid 3D reconstruction.
Non-rigid Structure from Motion techniques have been studied to perform monocular nonrigid 3D reconstruction.
Depth estimation is part of the joint problem of 3D reconstruction.
Non-rigid image registration is part of the joint problem of 3D reconstruction.
